chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has two vessels containing water, and filth fell into one of them, but he does not know which one it is, and he is not able to obtain any water other than it. He said: “He pours them both out and performs tayammum.”

key_terms.قَذَرٌ: filth or impurity that contaminates the water
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute for wudu (ablution) or ghusl
key_terms.يُهَرِيقُهُمَا: he pours both of them out

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if one of two water vessels is najis but he does not know which one?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity when a person has two containers of water and knows that one has been contaminated, but cannot identify which one. In such a case, and when no other water is available, both are discarded and tayammum is performed instead.
